newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO security chief says Hebron agreement close.
newsitem.headline: PLO security chief says Hebron agreement close.

text.p: Palestinian security chief Jibril Rajoub said on Friday he was "100 percent" certain Israel and the PLO would soon agree on a long-delayed Israeli redeployment in the West Bank town of Hebron.
"There is no choice but to reach an agreement...I am 100 percent certain that the two of us will soon arrive at an agreement," Rajoub told Israel's Army radio.

However, Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai confirmed in a newspaper interview printed on Friday that he wanted changes to the terms of the original Hebron agreement. Israel had denied Palestinian charges that it wanted to renegotiate the deal.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Israel would soon move towards final peace talks with the Palestinians and urged the Arab world to educate its children "not to hatred but brotherhood".
"Soon when we pass the present stage we will progress toward the discussions on the permanent arrangement," Netanyahu said at a memorial for fallen Israeli soldiers late on Thursday.

Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organisation have been holding U.S.-mediated negotiations on a partial Israeli pullback from Hebron in the West Bank, home to 400 Jewish settlers living in heavily armed compounds amid 100,000 Palestinians.

Spurred by a White House summit after clashes last month -- the most serious Israeli-Palestinian violence since peace deals were signed in 1993 -- negotiations began on Sunday on Israel's demand for better security for settlers.

Palestinians have opposed any reopening of the Hebron agreement reached with Israel's previous Labour-led government. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Thursday the talks at Erez checkpoint between Israel and self-ruled Gaza had achieved nothing.

U.S. Special Mideast Coordinator Dennis Ross, mediating the talks, said on Thursday Israel and the PLO had agreed to move negotiations to the Red Sea resorts of Eilat, in Israel, and nearby Taba, in Egypt. Ross said the change was to raise the pace of negotiations. Palestinans sources said talks would begin on Monday in Taba.

Israel said on Thursday it would ease a crippling closure of the West Bank and Gaza imposed after Moslem suicide attacks early this year and tightened after last month's clashes killed 60 Palestinians and 15 Israelis.

"Beginning this Sunday, about 35,000 workers from Judea, Samaria (the West Bank) and Gaza will be permitted to work in Israel and all internal closures in Judea and Samaria will be lifted, except for the city of Nablus," said a spokesman for Mordechai.

Some 60,000 Palestinians from the West Bank and the Gaza Strip worked in Israel before suicide bombings last February and March. Only 19,500 Palestinians worked in Israel before last month's violence.
It was unclear how long it would take Israel to carry out security checks and issue work permits to 35,000 labourers.
